To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed approach is able to detect direct discrimination, (2) the approach can be extended to detect indirect discrimination, (3) the proposed approach has a high degree of flexibility, and (4) the approach is applicable in real-world settings.

(1) we have formalized the problem of discovering direct and indirect discrimination through classification rule mining, (2) we have proposed and tested inference models to unveil indirect discrimination, and (3) we have shown that our approach is able to discover discrimination in the PKDD Challenge dataset, which is a real-world dataset of credit decisions

the use of classification rules for the discovery of discrimination in a dataset of decision records allows for unveiling contexts of discrimination, where the burden on the discriminated group is measured by the lift measure of the classification rule.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of discovering direct and indirect discrimination in a classification rule-based syntax and the proposal of two inference models that combine the extracted rules with background knowledge.
the development of data mining techniques for discovering contexts of direct or indirect discrimination, and for the assessment of the burden of such contexts on protected-by-law groups.
the development of a data mining framework for discovering discrimination in a dataset of decision records.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results show the effectiveness of data mining techniques for the fight against indirect discrimination.
our proposed inference models are able to unveil contexts of unlawful discrimination in the two datasets.
the proposed methodology is able to unveil contexts of discrimination in a classification rule-based representation of the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the fight against discrimination, data mining is an important tool that can be used to discover discrimination in historical decision records.

, given a dataset of historical decisions, we are able to discover discrimination in the form of classification rules that can be used as a starting point in the legal process for the fight against unfair discrimination.

, by means of data mining, we are able to discover discrimination in a dataset of decision records, by means of a set of classification rules, that are extracted automatically from the data, and by means of a background knowledge, that can be provided in the form of a census or of other data sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data mining can be a useful tool in the hands of lawyers and civil rights activists in their fight against discrimination.
data mining techniques, in conjunction with background knowledge, can be a powerful tool for unveiling unlawful discrimination in decision support systems.
data mining techniques can be used to support the fight against discrimination, by providing tools for the discovery of discrimination in historical decision records.
